summary.headline: Belrise Q1 FY27 PAT rose 9% YoY to INR1,217 million on 13% revenue growth to INR25,465 million; EBITDA margin 11.5%.
summary.overview: Consolidated total revenue rose 13% YoY to INR25,465 million and manufacturing revenue grew 20% to INR21,979 million. EBITDA grew 5% to INR2,933 million at an 11.5% margin, with manufacturing EBITDA up 10% at a 12.7% margin, while PAT rose 9% to INR1,217 million. Management said raw material, staff and energy cost pressures peaked in Q1 and guided to FY26-level EBITDA margins, while the trading business fell about 19% YoY on Middle East disruption. The company completed a INR17,000 million QIP, announced the HYVA India tipper business acquisition (closing expected Q3 FY27), and won several new orders.

financial_highlights.metric: Manufacturing revenue mix: two- and three-wheeler
Manufacturing revenue mix: passenger vehicle / commercial vehicle / others

segments.name: Two- and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: About 81.4% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27. Management said revenue grew about 18% YoY, below industry volume growth of roughly 20-25%, which it attributed to customer mix. New wins include a chassis order worth over INR650 million annually from a fast-growing OEM, plus an INR500 million annual chassis program from a large OEM.

segments.name: Four-wheeler and commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: Management said revenue grew 18% YoY in Q1. Commercial vehicle contributed 8.5% and passenger vehicle 4.6% of manufacturing revenue. Won an order for 59 assemblies for a leading Indian commercial four-wheeler OEM's EV localization program, plus tooling and automation design work.

segments.name: Renewable energy and aerospace/defence (other revenue)
segments.commentary: Small base and volatile; management expects it to be the fastest-growing segment. Won a sheet metal assembly order for a US solar tracker maker supporting about 2.5 GW of annual supply, with peak annual revenue above INR1,500 million from Q4 FY27. Management targets aerospace and defence at at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

segments.name: Trading business
segments.commentary: Revenue fell about 19% YoY in Q1 due to Middle East crisis effects on logistics and demand, mainly for African, Asian and Middle Eastern markets. Management expects growth, though slower than manufacturing.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated revenue guidance: mid-teens growth with stable EBITDA margins.
EBITDA margin expected to remain broadly stable versus FY26 levels; management does not expect a material margin impact this fiscal year.
Commodity, staff and energy/transport cost pressures described as largely peaked, with pass-through to customers expected in coming quarters.
Most of the INR17,000 million QIP proceeds to be deployed within FY27, mainly for inorganic opportunities in aerospace and four-wheeler/commercial vehicle, plus some organic growth.
HYVA India tipper business acquisition expected to complete in Q3 FY27; it also brings three manufacturing facilities in Pune, Jamshedpur and Bangalore.
New programs (Bangalore chassis, US solar tracker assemblies, brake assemblies, Sambhajinagar chassis) expected to start production in Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: Four new facilities are coming up, including brownfield sites; fixed costs from ramp-up hiring are hitting P&L before revenue.

Bangalore brownfield facility to host the new two-wheeler chassis program (start of production Q4 FY27); management declined to disclose utilisation or ramp for specific facilities, including Haridwar.
US solar tracker assembly expansion to support about 2.5 GW of annual supply; production from Q4 FY27 with gradual ramp.
Expansion at existing Maharashtra facilities for the commercial four-wheeler EV localization program.
HYVA tipper acquisition brings three facilities (Pune, Jamshedpur, Bangalore).
H-One Japan technology collaboration concluded, enabling high tensile steel up to 1470 MPa, about 3x the current Indian industry standard.
demand_pricing: Back-to-back pricing lets steel and polymer cost changes pass to customers with a lag; management said commodity pass-through is expected in the coming quarters.
Q1 cost headwinds: elevated steel, polymer, energy and logistics costs from the global oil situation, plus higher staff costs after the minimum wage hike and the annual increment cycle.

Two-wheeler OEM content per vehicle rising: fuel tanks, exhaust, chassis, suspension and braking; cumulative annual run rate of about INR2,000 million with this OEM including suspension and braking wins.
Suspension supplied to four two/three-wheeler OEMs, with a fifth (a Vietnamese two-wheeler maker entering India) added this quarter for suspension and braking.
Management said a China replacement strategy is driving global OEMs and Tier 1s to India, citing IP, governance and capability.
Plasan Sasa: Belrise already exports parts to Israel; progress is gradual given geopolitical conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new two-wheeler chassis order (INR650 million) on top of earlier wins, and what is the cumulative run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is over and above the exhaust and fuel tank wins from last quarter (about INR900 million). Cumulative chassis, exhaust and fuel tank wins total about INR1,550 million annual run rate; with suspension and braking, the OEM run rate is about INR2,000 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is the renewable energy sheet metal revenue recurring, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is recurring, the first order from a North American solar tracker maker, starting in Q4 FY27 with gradual ramp. Initial 2.5 GW is an entry point and can expand to export and domestic opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins evolve given commodity, staff and energy cost pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the worst of commodity, staff, and energy/transport cost pressure is behind them. Pass-through is expected in coming quarters and margins should be maintained at FY26 levels. Staff costs rose ahead of new facility ramp-ups and have largely peaked.

qa_highlights.question: Why did two/three-wheeler revenue growth (about 18%) lag industry growth (about 20-25%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a customer mix issue: some faster-growing OEMs it does not work with closely gained share. It expects wins at newly penetrated OEMs to flow into Q3 and Q4 FY27. Management declined to quantify the raw material pass-through benefit, to be answered offline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the trading business outlook after the roughly 19% decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Middle East disruption hit African, Asian and Middle Eastern trade from April to June and it expects normalisation. No segment guidance was given; company-wide guidance is mid-teens revenue growth with stable EBITDA margins.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is expected from aerospace and defence, and will it be disclosed separately?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a target of at least 10% of manufacturing revenue from aerospace and defence in the short to medium term. It agreed to consider carving out defence and aerospace revenue from other revenue in future disclosures.

risks_watch: Recovery of the trading business is uncertain given Middle East disruption; no segment guidance was given.
Margin outlook depends on commodity pass-through timing and on ramp-up of four new facilities, which front-loads fixed costs.
Execution risk on deploying about INR17,000 million QIP proceeds into acquisitions; return thresholds are EPS and ROCE accretive from day one.
HYVA tipper acquisition (announced 4 August 2026) still needs to close in Q3 FY27.
Two/three-wheeler growth lagging industry; management said new OEM ramp-ups should show in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Geopolitical exposure: Israel-linked defence work (Plasan Sasa) is progressing gradually; the Middle East situation affects trading and logistics.
Management declined to disclose facility-level utilisation, the RM pass-through benefit, and segment-level H-One and Mag filters numbers. Some details were promised offline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term story and cost recovery, with repeated statements that the "worst is behind us" on costs. Evasive on specifics: declined facility utilisation, RM pass-through quantum, trading guidance and H-One/Mag filters numbers, deferring some to offline discussion.
key_quotes: I can say with a great amount of confidence that the worst is behind us in terms of cost pressures.
We expect EBITDA margins to remain broadly stable as compared to FY26 levels.
Once you are already in, secured the supplies for a product for any of the models, it's far easier to replicate horizontally and expand that portfolio across different models.

adds.what: Four new facilities coming up incl. brownfield sites (Bangalore brownfield for two-wheeler chassis program)
US solar tracker assembly expansion supporting ~2.5 GW annual supply
HYVA India tipper acquisition bringing three manufacturing facilities (Pune, Jamshedpur, Bangalore), closing Q3 FY27
Expansion at existing Maharashtra facilities for commercial four-wheeler EV localization program

growth.why: Management reiterated mid-teens consolidated revenue growth with broadly stable EBITDA margins vs FY26; backing is partial, with named programs (Bangalore chassis, US solar tracker ~2.5 GW, Maharashtra EV expansion, HYVA acquisition closing Q3 FY27) and new orders, but no utilisation or per-facility ramp disclosed and trading revenue fell ~19%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided EBITDA margin broadly stable vs FY26 (Q1 manufacturing EBITDA margin 12.7%, consolidated 11.5%), with no margin expansion targeted; cost pressures described as peaked but pass-through lags.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Four new facilities under construction; Bangalore chassis, US solar tracker (~2.5 GW, peak revenue above INR1,500 million) and Sambhajinagar chassis programs start production in Q4 FY27, with HYVA's three plants adding at Q3 FY27 closing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Manufacturing revenue grew 20% YoY to INR21,979 million; two/three-wheeler up ~18% with new OEM wins expected to ramp in Q3-Q4 FY27 and new programs starting Q4 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: INR17,000 million QIP completed with most proceeds to be deployed within FY27 for inorganic aerospace and four-wheeler/CV opportunities, and brownfield expansions already under way; utilisation not disclosed, so the read is from deployment plans rather than utilisation.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance held at mid-teens revenue growth and broadly stable EBITDA margins; Q1 revenue grew 13% consolidated, below the mid-teens guide, and trading fell ~19%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consolidated revenue growth of 13% in Q1 sits just below mid-teens guide, trading revenue fell ~19%, and fixed costs from four facilities hit P&L before revenue ramps; EBITDA grew only 5% vs revenue 13%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New programs (Bangalore two-wheeler chassis, US solar tracker assemblies, brake assemblies, Sambhajinagar chassis) expected to start production in Q4 FY27, and H-One Japan tech enables 1470 MPa high tensile steel.

rows.label: Two/three-wheeler OEM content wins ramping
rows.why: Cumulative OEM run rate about INR2,000 million including suspension and braking; new chassis order over INR650 million annually on top of ~INR900 million earlier wins.

rows.label: HYVA India tipper acquisition closing
rows.why: Announced 4 August 2026 and expected to complete in Q3 FY27, bringing three manufacturing facilities in Pune, Jamshedpur and Bangalore.

rows.label: Aerospace and defence at 10% of revenue
rows.why: Management targets at least 10% of consolidated revenue from A&D in the medium term, but Plasan Sasa progress is gradual given geopolitical conditions and the current base is small.

tone.note: Management was confident that the worst of commodity, staff and energy cost pressure is behind it and that medium-term growth is intact, but was evasive on facility utilisation, RM pass-through quantum, trading guidance and some H-One/Mag filter numbers; analysts pushed on the two-wheeler growth lag

quality.why: Manufacturing revenue grew 20% (INR18,323m to INR21,979m) with two/three-wheeler up about 18% and four-wheeler/CV up about 18%, driven by new OEM wins and customer ramp-ups, while the trading business fell about 19%; the brief lists no one-off gains, losses, or low-base effects, and the HYVA acquisition has not yet closed so it adds nothing to Q1 growth.
